question.problem:
The following table gives the values of functions $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ at some points. Find $({f}^{-1})^{′}(4).$

| **$x$** | $f(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-2$ | $1$ | $4$ |
| $1$ | $4$ | $-2$ |
question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=4,$ we have

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${f}^{-1}(4)=1$ and ${f}^{′}(1)=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(4) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(4))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(1)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
